title: Hypercohomology on a qcqs scheme commutes with bounded-below filtered colimits
statement:
Let $Y$ be a qcqs scheme, $A$ a sheaf of rings on $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$, and let
$W_\bullet\to Y$ be a hypercovering by affine weakly contractible objects with each $W_n$
quasi-compact (a finite disjoint union of affines).

1. An additive functor $\Phi$ between Grothendieck abelian categories that is exact and
   commutes with arbitrary direct sums commutes with all small colimits; in particular
   $M\mapsto M(W_n)$, from $A$-modules to abelian groups, commutes with filtered colimits.
2. For a complex $K^\bullet$ of $A$-modules vanishing in degrees $<a$,
   $H^q(Y,K^\bullet)=H^q\operatorname{Tot}(K^m(W_n))_{m,n}$, and the degree-$q$ term
   $\bigoplus_{n+m=q,\,n\ge0,\,m\ge a}K^m(W_n)$ of the total complex is a finite direct sum.
3. For a filtered diagram $(K_i^\bullet)$ of such complexes with a common $a$, the map
   $\varinjlim_iH^q(Y,K_i^\bullet)\to H^q(Y,\varinjlim_iK_i^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Colimit presentation, including the empty diagram. Let $D:J\to\mathcal C$ be a small diagram in an abelian category with small coproducts, and write $P=\bigoplus_{j\in J}D_j$ and $Q=\bigoplus_{u:j\to k}D_j$. Define $t:Q\to P$ on the summand indexed by $u:j\to k$ by $\iota_j-\iota_kD(u)$. For any object $B$, a map $P\to B$ is a family $b_j:D_j\to B$, and its composite with $t$ is zero exactly when $b_j=b_kD(u)$ for every $u$. Thus maps $\operatorname{coker}(t)\to B$ are exactly cocones from $D$ to $B$, uniquely, so $\operatorname{coker}(t)$ is the colimit, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The required coproducts exist for a Grothendieck abelian category by [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and cokernels exist by [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: paragraph (1), cokernel presentation; universal-property verification written out

proof.text: Proof of the general assertion in (1). Apply the preceding presentation in the source and target of $\Phi$. By [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a), exactness makes $\Phi(\operatorname{coker}t)$ a cokernel of $\Phi(t)$. The assumed coproduct comparisons identify $\Phi(Q)$ and $\Phi(P)$ with the coproducts of $\Phi(D_j)$ indexed by the same arrows and objects. Additivity identifies the component of $\Phi(t)$ with $\iota_j-\iota_k\Phi(D(u))$. Hence its cokernel, with the images of the original cocone legs, is the colimit of $\Phi D$ by step 1. This proves preservation of every small colimit, with its canonical comparison map.

source.place: Tag 010N, label lemma-exact-functor, cokernel preservation; application to blueprint proof paragraph (1)

proof.text: Evaluation clause of (1). Apply [det-proper-heart-continuity-sections] with the ambient scheme $Y$, the given arbitrary sheaf of rings $A$, and $W=W_n$. Its statement gives exactness and preservation of all colimits for evaluation into abelian groups, hence in particular the required filtered colimits. The hypotheses hold separately for each $n$: $W_n$ is affine and weakly contractible by assumption. This uses the statement of an existing node, and requires neither a choice of a new cover nor a constant or commutative coefficient ring.

source.place: paragraph (1), evaluation on each affine weakly contractible term; existing same-unit sections lemma

proof.text: Hypercover computation and (2). Apply [det-pe-hypercover-complex] to the given hypercover $W_\bullet\to Y$, with $U=Y$, $\mathcal R=A$ and the given integer lower bound $a$. It gives, naturally in $K$, $R\Gamma(Y,K)\simeq T(K)$, where $T(K)^q=\bigoplus_{n+m=q,\,n\ge0,\,m\ge a}K^m(W_n)$ and the differential on the $(n,m)$ summand is $\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^jd_j^*+(-1)^nd_K$. Taking $q$-th cohomology proves the displayed identification in (2). The conditions on a contributing pair are exactly $m=q-n$ and $0\le n\le q-a$, so there are finitely many summands; if $q<a$ the sum is empty and is zero. The hypercover lemma applies to any such given hypercover; its existence assertion is not being used to replace this one. Here $H^q(Y,K)$ means $H^q(R\Gamma(Y,K))$, with the derived-functor convention of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and the cohomology convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a possibly negative $a$, the first-quadrant totalization recipe of [def-sp-double-complex-total] is applied after reindexing the second coordinate by $b=m-a\ge0$; its total degree $n+b$ is relabelled as $q=a+n+b$. This relabelling changes no differential: its component remains $\delta+(-1)^n d_K$. Thus no assumption $a\ge0$ and no additional cochain-shift sign is introduced.

source.place: paragraph (2); Stacks Tag 09A2, proetale-lemma-compute-cohomology, as exposed by the existing bounded-complex hypercover node

proof.text:
Commutation on complexes. Form $K=\varinjlim_iK_i$ degree by degree with differential induced by the $d_{K_i}$. Below $a$ each diagram is zero, whose colimit is zero by the cocone universal property, so $K$ has the same lower bound. By [det-proper-heart-continuity-sections] the canonical maps $\varinjlim_iK_i^m(W_n)\to K^m(W_n)$ are isomorphisms. Consequently, for each $q$, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$\theta^q:\varinjlim_i\bigoplus_{0\le n\le q-a}K_i^{q-n}(W_n)\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \bigoplus_{0\le n\le q-a}K^{q-n}(W_n).$$
Here interchange of coproduct and colimit follows directly from [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: maps from either object into $B$ are families of maps $K_i^{q-n}(W_n)\to B$ compatible in $i$, separately for every $n$. On each summand $\theta$ is induced by the structural map $K_i^m\to K^m$. These maps commute with $d_K$ because they are chain maps, and commute with every face restriction $d_j^*$ because they are maps of sheaves. They therefore commute with the displayed signed total differential. Thus $\theta:\varinjlim_i T(K_i)\to T(K)$ is an isomorphism of complexes, with the colimit on the left computed degreewise. The latter description also follows from the same universal property: compatible degreewise maps form a chain map precisely when they commute with each differential.

source.place: paragraph (3), evaluation, finite diagonal sum, and both differentials; universal-property details written out

proof.text:
Exact filtered colimits give cohomology commutation. Put $T_i=T(K_i)$, $Z_i^q=\ker(d:T_i^q\to T_i^{q+1})$, $B_i^q=\operatorname{im}(d:T_i^{q-1}\to T_i^q)$ and $H_i^q=Z_i^q/B_i^q$, as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Chain maps make these diagrams in abelian groups. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] to the compatible exact sequences
$$0\to Z_i^q\to T_i^q\to B_i^{q+1}\to0,\qquad 0\to B_i^q\to T_i^q,\qquad 0\to B_i^q\to Z_i^q\to H_i^q\to0.$$
The outgoing differential factors as $\varinjlim_iT_i^q\twoheadrightarrow\varinjlim_iB_i^{q+1}\hookrightarrow\varinjlim_iT_i^{q+1}$: the first sequence gives the surjection and identifies its kernel with $\varinjlim_iZ_i^q$, and the second sequence in degree $q+1$ makes the last arrow injective. Thus the kernel of the outgoing differential is precisely $\varinjlim_iZ_i^q$. Likewise $\varinjlim_iB_i^q$ is the image of the incoming differential: the map $\varinjlim_iT_i^{q-1}\to\varinjlim_iB_i^q$ is surjective by the first sequence in degree $q-1$, and the boundary inclusions stay injective by the second sequence. The third then identifies the quotient of cycles by boundaries with $\varinjlim_iH_i^q$. Hence the canonical map $\varinjlim_iH^q(T_i)\to H^q(\varinjlim_iT_i)$ is an isomorphism. This only uses exactness for a small filtered diagram; no interchange of an infinite limit or a spectral-sequence convergence assertion is needed.

source.place: Tag 00DB, label lemma-directed-colimit-exact; apply the exactness statement of the existing small-filtered-category node to cycles and boundaries

proof.text: Identification of the map in (3). For every cocone leg $K_i\to K$, naturality in [det-pe-hypercover-complex] identifies $H^q(Y,K_i)\to H^q(Y,K)$ with $H^q(T(K_i))\to H^q(T(K))$. The composite of the isomorphism of step 6 with $H^q(\theta)$ of step 5 agrees on the $i$-th cocone leg with this same map, since $\theta$ was defined by those legs. By the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], after the identifications of step 4 this composite is exactly the canonical map $\varinjlim_iH^q(Y,K_i)\to H^q(Y,\varinjlim_iK_i)$. It is an isomorphism, proving (3) for every integer $q$.
